ESV.1: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel, but he incurred guilt through Baal and died.
ESV.2: And now they sin more and more, and make for themselves metal images, idols skillfully made of their silver, all of them the work of craftsmen. It is said of them, “Those who offer human sacrifice kiss calves!”
ESV.3: Therefore they shall be like the morning mist or like the dew that goes early away, like the chaff that swirls from the threshing floor or like smoke from a window.
ESV.4: But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; you know no God but me, and besides me there is no savior.
ESV.5: It was I who knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought;
ESV.6: but when they had grazed,  they became full, they were filled, and their heart was lifted up; therefore they forgot me.
ESV.7: So I am to them like a lion; like a leopard I will lurk beside the way.
ESV.8: I will fall upon them like a bear robbed of her cubs; I will tear open their breast, and there I will devour them like a lion, as a wild beast would rip them open.
ESV.9: He destroys  you, O Israel, for you are against me, against your helper.
ESV.10: Where now is your king, to save you in all your cities? Where are all your rulers — those of whom you said, “Give me a king and princes”?
ESV.11: I gave you a king in my anger, and I took him away in my wrath.
ESV.12: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is kept in store.
ESV.13: The pangs of childbirth come for him, but he is an unwise son, for at the right time he does not present himself at the opening of the womb.
ESV.14: I shall ransom them from the power of Sheol; I shall redeem them from Death.  O Death, where are your plagues? O Sheol, where is your sting? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.
ESV.15: Though he may flourish among his brothers, the east wind, the wind of the LORD, shall come, rising from the wilderness, and his fountain shall dry up; his spring shall be parched; it shall strip his treasury of every precious thing.
ESV.16: Samaria shall bear her guilt, because she has rebelled against her God; they shall fall by the sword; their little ones shall be dashed in pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.

NASB.1: When Ephraim spoke, [there was] trembling. He exalted himself in Israel, But through Baal he did wrong and died.
NASB.2: And now they sin more and more, And make for themselves molten images, Idols skillfully made from their silver, All of them the work of craftsmen. They say of them, 'Let the men who sacrifice kiss the calves!'
NASB.3: Therefore they will be like the morning cloud And like dew which soon disappears, Like chaff which is blown away from the threshing floor And like smoke from a chimney.
NASB.4: Yet I [have been] the LORD your God Since the land of Egypt; And you were not to know any god except Me, For there is no savior besides Me.
NASB.5: I cared for you in the wilderness, In the land of drought.
NASB.6: As [they had] their pasture, they became satisfied, And being satisfied, their heart became proud; Therefore they forgot Me.

NASB.8: I will encounter them like a bear robbed of her cubs, And I will tear open their chests; There I will also devour them like a lioness, [As] a wild beast would tear them.

NASB.10: Where now is your king That he may save you in all your cities, And your judges of whom you requested, 'Give me a king and princes '?

NASB.12: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; His sin is stored up.

NASB.15: Though he flourishes among the reeds, An east wind will come, The wind of the LORD coming up from the wilderness; And his fountain will become dry And his spring will be dried up; It will plunder [his] treasury of every precious article.
NASB.16: Samaria will be held guilty, For she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword, Their little ones will be dashed in pieces, And their pregnant women will be ripped open.

NLT.1:
When the tribe of Ephraim spoke,
the people shook with fear,
for that tribe was important in Israel.
But the people of Ephraim sinned by worshiping Baal
and thus sealed their destruction.
NLT.2:
Now they continue to sin by making silver idols,
images shaped skillfully with human hands.
“Sacrifice to these,” they cry,
“and kiss the calf idols!”
NLT.3:
Therefore, they will disappear like the morning mist,
like dew in the morning sun,
like chaff blown by the wind,
like smoke from a chimney.
NLT.4:
“I have been the LORD your God
ever since I brought you out of Egypt.
You must acknowledge no God but me,
for there is no other savior.
NLT.5:
I took care of you in the wilderness,
in that dry and thirsty land.
NLT.6:
But when you had eaten and were satisfied,
you became proud and forgot me.
NLT.7:
So now I will attack you like a lion,
like a leopard that lurks along the road.
NLT.8:
Like a bear whose cubs have been taken away,
I will tear out your heart.
I will devour you like a hungry lioness
and mangle you like a wild animal.
NLT.9:
“You are about to be destroyed, O Israel —
yes, by me, your only helper.
NLT.10:
Now where is your king?
Let him save you!
Where are all the leaders of the land,
the king and the officials you demanded of me?
NLT.11:
In my anger I gave you kings,
and in my fury I took them away.
NLT.12:
“Ephraim’s guilt has been collected,
and his sin has been stored up for punishment.
NLT.13:
Pain has come to the people
like the pain of childbirth,
but they are like a child
who resists being born.
The moment of birth has arrived,
but they stay in the womb!
NLT.14:
“Should I ransom them from the grave ?
Should I redeem them from death?
O death, bring on your terrors!
O grave, bring on your plagues!
For I will not take pity on them.
NLT.15:
Ephraim was the most fruitful of all his brothers,
but the east wind — a blast from the LORD —
will arise in the desert.
All their flowing springs will run dry,
and all their wells will disappear.
Every precious thing they own
will be plundered and carried away.
NLT.16:
The people of Samaria
must bear the consequences of their guilt
because they rebelled against their God.
They will be killed by an invading army,
their little ones dashed to death against the ground,
their pregnant women ripped open by swords.”

AMP.1:
When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling and terror.
He exalted himself [above the other tribes] in Israel;
But through [the worship of] Baal he became guilty and died [spiritually, and then came ruin, sealing Israel's doom as a nation].
AMP.2:
And now they sin more and more,
And make for themselves molten images,
Idols skillfully made from their silver [as it pleased them],
All of them the work of the craftsmen.
They say of these [very works of their hands], "Let those who sacrifice kiss and show respect to the calves [as if they were living gods]!"
AMP.3:
Therefore they will be [swiftly dissipated] like the morning cloud
Or like dew which soon disappears,
Like chaff which swirls with the whirlwind from the threshing floor,
And like smoke from the chimney or through the window [worthless and without substance —they will vanish].
AMP.4:
Yet I have been the LORD your God
Since [the time you became a nation in] the land of Egypt;
And you were not to know any god except Me,
For there is no savior besides Me.
AMP.5:
I knew and regarded you and cared for you in the wilderness,
In the land of drought.
AMP.6:
When they had their pasture, they became satisfied,
And being satisfied, their heart became proud (self-centered);
Therefore they forgot Me.
AMP.7:
So I will be like a lion to them;
Like a leopard I will watch and lie in wait [ready to attack] by the road [to Assyria].
AMP.8:
I will encounter them like a bear robbed of her cubs,
And I will tear open their chests;
There I will also devour them like a lioness,
As a wild beast would tear them.
AMP.9:
It is your destruction, O Israel,
Because you are against Me, [and have rebelled] against your help.
AMP.10:
Where now is your king
That he may save you [when you are attacked] in all your cities?
And your judges of whom you asked,
"Give me a king and princes"?
AMP.11:
I gave you a king in My anger,
And I took him away in My wrath [as punishment].
AMP.12:
The wickedness of Ephraim [which is not yet completely punished] is bound up [as in a bag];
His sin is stored up [for judgment and destruction].
AMP.13:
The pains of childbirth come on him;
But he is not a wise son,
For it is not the time to delay [his chance at a new birth] as the womb opens [but he ignores the opportunity to change].
AMP.14:
Shall I ransom them from the power of Sheol (the place of the dead)?
Shall I redeem them from death?
O death, where are your thorns?
O Sheol, where is your sting?
Compassion is hidden from My eyes [because of their failure to repent].
AMP.15:
For though he flourishes among the reeds (his fellow tribes),
An east wind (Assyria) will come,
The breath of the LORD rising from the desert;
And Ephraim's spring will become dry
And his fountain will be dried up.
Assyria will plunder his treasury of every precious object.
AMP.16:
Samaria will be found guilty [and become desolate],
Because she rebelled against her God;
They will fall by the sword,
Their infants will be dashed in pieces,
And their pregnant women will be ripped open.

he was exalted in Israel.

they make idols for themselves from their silver,
cleverly fashioned images,
all of them the work of craftsmen.

NIV.3:
Therefore they will be like the morning mist,
like the early dew that disappears,
like chaff swirling from a threshing floor,
like smoke escaping through a window.
NIV.4:
“But I am the Lord your God,
who brought you out of Egypt.

no Savior except me.
NIV.5:

in the land of burning heat.
NIV.6:

when they were satisfied, they became proud;
then they forgot me.

like a leopard I will lurk by the path.
NIV.8:
Like a bear robbed of her cubs,
I will attack them and rip them open.

a wild animal will tear them apart.
NIV.9:
“You are destroyed, O Israel,
because you are against me, against your helper.

MSG.1:
God once let loose against Ephraim
a terrifying sentence against Israel:
Caught and convicted
in the lewd sex-worship of Baal—they died!
MSG.2:
And now they're back in the sin business again,
manufacturing god-images they can use,
Religion customized to taste. Professionals see to it:
Anything you want in a god you can get.
Can you believe it? They sacrifice live babies to these dead gods—
kill living babies and kiss golden calves!
MSG.3:
And now there's nothing left to these people:
hollow men, desiccated women,
Like scraps of paper blown down the street,
like smoke in a gusty wind.
MSG.4:
"I'm still your God,
the God who saved you out of Egypt.
I'm the only real God you've ever known.
I'm the one and only God who delivers.
MSG.5:
I took care of you during the wilderness hard times,
those years when you had nothing.
MSG.6:
I took care of you, took care of all your needs,
gave you everything you needed.
You were spoiled. You thought you didn't need me.
You forgot me.
MSG.7:
"I'll charge them like a lion,
like a leopard stalking in the brush.
MSG.8:
I'll jump them like a sow grizzly robbed of her cubs.
I'll rip out their guts.
Coyotes will make a meal of them.
Crows will clean their bones.
MSG.9:
I'm going to destroy you, Israel.
Who is going to stop me?
MSG.10:
Where is your trusty king you thought would save you?
Where are all the local leaders you wanted so badly?
All these rulers you insisted on having,
demanding, 'Give me a king! Give me leaders!'?
MSG.11:
Well, long ago I gave you a king, but I wasn't happy about it.
Now, fed up, I've gotten rid of him.
MSG.12:

Ephraim's sin documented and stored in a safe-deposit box.
MSG.13:

MSG.14:

Shall I snatch them from a certain death?

banishing sorrow,

NET.1: When Ephraim spoke, there was terror; he was exalted in Israel, but he became guilty by worshiping Baal and died.
NET.2: Even now they persist in sin! They make metal images for themselves, idols that they skillfully fashion from their own silver; all of them are nothing but the work of craftsmen! There is a saying about them: “Those who sacrifice to the calf idol are calf kissers!”
NET.3: Therefore they will disappear like the morning mist, like early morning dew that evaporates, like chaff that is blown away from a threshing floor, like smoke that disappears through an open window.
NET.4: But I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt. Therefore, you must not acknowledge any God but me; except me there is no Savior.
NET.5: I cared for you in the wilderness, in the dry desert where no water was.
NET.6: When they were fed, they became satisfied; when they were satisfied, they became proud; as a result, they forgot me!
NET.7: So I will pounce on them like a lion; like a leopard I will lurk by the path.
NET.8: I will attack them like a bear robbed of her cubs — I will rip open their chests. I will devour them there like a lion — like a wild animal would tear them apart.
NET.9: I will destroy you, O Israel! Who is there to help you?
NET.10: Where then is your king, that he may save you in all your cities? Where are your rulers for whom you asked, saying, “Give me a king and princes”?
NET.11: I granted you a king in my anger, and I will take him away in my wrath!
NET.12: The punishment of Ephraim has been decreed; his punishment is being stored up for the future.
NET.13: The labor pains of a woman will overtake him, but the baby will lack wisdom; when the time arrives, he will not come out of the womb!
NET.14: Will I deliver them from the power of Sheol? No, I will not! Will I redeem them from death? No, I will not! O Death, bring on your plagues! O Sheol, bring on your destruction! My eyes will not show any compassion!
NET.15: Even though he flourishes like a reed plant, a scorching east wind will come, a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert. As a result, his spring will dry up; his well will become dry. That wind will spoil all his delightful foods in the containers in his storehouse.
NET.16: (14:1) Samaria will be held guilty, because she rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword, their infants will be dashed to the ground — their pregnant women will be ripped open.
